city_center.name: Eastern Market (Capitol Hill) + Union Market (NoMa)
city_center.landmark: Eastern Market (1873), DC's oldest continuously operating public market; the National Mall; Capitol Hill rowhouses; Northern Virginia suburbs (Arlington, Alexandria, Fairfax)
city_center.notes: Eastern Market on Capitol Hill is DC's historic public market, with a weekend farmers line and local producers. Union Market is a modern food hall in NoMa. The metro extends across the Potomac into Northern Virginia. sources: easternmarket-dc.org; en.wikipedia.org Eastern Market (Washington, D.C.).

cultural_notes: Eastern Market (1873) is DC's oldest continuously operating public market, a Capitol Hill civic anchor with a weekend farmers line (source: en.wikipedia.org Eastern Market; easternmarket-dc.org)
the DC metro holds one of the largest Ethiopian communities in the US, centered on the U Street / Shaw corridor and Silver Spring (source: general community framing, publicly documented)

Northern Virginia is a large, food-diverse suburban wing of the metro; Salvadoran pupuserias and the Eden Center Vietnamese hub are notable food landmarks (source: publicly documented metro food geography)

Wegmans, Harris Teeter, Giant, and Safeway are the metro's grocery chains; Shenandoah Valley farm country supplies apples and produce (source: chain regional footprint; Virginia apple growers framing)
